questions.question: 6. A differential protection protect transformer from the following fault-

answers.a: Over current due to overloads and external short circuits

explanations.a: Incorrect. Differential protection does not respond to external faults or overloads (through fault condition).
explanations.b: Incorrect. Small interturn faults may not be detected by differential protection.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Oil leakage is detected by Buchholz relay, not differential protection.
explanations.d: Correct. Differential protection detects incipient internal faults (winding insulation breakdown, core faults, etc.) that cause current imbalance.

questions.question: 7. How does the tap changing effect of transformer can be nullify in differential protection of transformer:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Changing CT ratios for each tap position is impractical.
explanations.b: Correct. Percentage differential relay uses a restraining coil (bias coil) to desensitize the relay for through faults and tap changing effects.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Tappings in relay coil is not standard practice.
explanations.d: Incorrect because restraining coil is the correct method.

questions.question: 8. In pole mounted substation, which protection is used:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Differential protection is used for large transformers (>5 MVA), not for pole mounted substations.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Earth fault protection may be present but is not the primary answer.
explanations.c: Correct. Pole mounted substations (distribution transformers up to 100-200 kVA) typically use Dropout (DO) fuses for protection.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Buchholz relay is used on oil filled transformers above 500 kVA with conservator tanks.

questions.question: 9. The differential protection is used for which type of transformer:

explanations.a: Partial. Differential protection is used for oil cooled transformers above 5 MVA.
explanations.b: Partial. Also used for air cooled (dry type) transformers above certain rating.
explanations.c: Partial. Also used for SF6 cooled transformers.
explanations.d: Correct. Differential protection can be applied to any type of transformer (oil cooled, air cooled, SF6 cooled) regardless of cooling medium, provided the rating justifies it.

questions.question: 10. In differential protection the relay is connected:

answers.c: At equipotential point of pilot wire

explanations.a: Incorrect. The relay is not necessarily near the CT.
explanations.c: Correct. The differential relay is connected at the equipotential point of the pilot wires (the common point where secondary currents from both CTs are compared).
